title: Fresh analysis auto-saves silently — no receipt, no link to /history/[slug], and the verdict-recording surface (DispositionEditor) is a hidden hop away
expected: After a run, an explicit confirmation of what happened and to whom: 'saved as <slug>' with a link to the saved report, where advance/hold/pass can be recorded (Petra's no-silent-success criterion).
got: runAnalyze persists every successful analysis (analyze-run.ts:184,214-234) and returns a persistence receipt in the payload (schemas.ts:72-76), but the result UI never shows it: analysis.persistence.slug is consumed only by the GitHub PATCH (useAnalyzeForm.ts:291) and the Tasks tab link (TasksTab.tsx:510-512). DispositionEditor exists only on /history/[slug] (app/history/[slug]/page.tsx:133-137), which the fresh result does not link.
l2_priority: Live: finish a run, then observe how a user discovers the saved report and records a disposition; time the detour. Confirm no receipt is rendered anywhere on the fresh result.
suggested_acceptance: The result panel header shows 'Uloženo jako <slug>' linking to /history/[slug], and (ideally) offers the disposition control inline on the fresh result.
scope_note: Overlaps backlog idea-f64e941d (give every silent success a receipt) — not in accepted-gaps.md, so surfaced.

title: Decision-layer strings are engine English inside the Czech report (trust ledger, soft-signal probes, interview kit, evidence trace)
expected: A report Petra hands a Czech line manager reads in Czech end to end; the LLM narrative already honors --lang.
got: The LLM narrative is localized (gemini.py:529) but the deterministic layers are English by construction and shown verbatim: sanity-check sentences (QualityStrip.tsx:13-16 'deterministic engine English'), soft-signal labels/probes (SoftSignalsSection.tsx:15, checklist lines '[RED FLAG] …'), interview-kit question/scaffold templates (interview.py:55-80), evidence-trace strings (insights.py:81-91).
l2_priority: Live: render a cs report and count English decision-layer strings visible on one screen (QualityStrip warns + Interview tab); judge whether a Czech manager could read the packet unaided.
suggested_acceptance: Deterministic engine strings are emitted as i18n keys (or localized server-side by lang) so a cs report is cs throughout; skill/technology names stay verbatim.
scope_note: Also hits Eva when defending to a Czech director; judged once here.

title: 'Independent' keyword-coverage check is bounded by a tech-dominant taxonomy — structurally thin for Petra's non-tech ČS requisitions
expected: For a branch-advisor / retail-ops JD, the coverage panel surfaces the JD's real keyword universe (banking products, client service, MS Office, sales targets…).
got: With no authoritative job_skills passed (pipeline.py:251-264), coverage harvests JD keywords from the taxonomy's skill pool only (ats.py:63,192-194; taxonomy.py:272-283). data/taxonomy.json's skill terms are overwhelmingly software/devops/data (python…kafka; the only finance-adjacent ids are role markers like role_banker), so a non-tech ČS JD yields a near-empty pool and a coverage percent computed over almost nothing.
l2_priority: Live: analyze a CV against a ČS branch-advisor JD; check whether the keyword-coverage panel is empty/trivial and whether its % reads as meaningful when it is not.
suggested_acceptance: Coverage is either fed the JD's structured requirements when a saved JD is picked, or the taxonomy grows domain terms for the seeded ČS families; an under-populated pool states 'compared against N known terms'.
scope_note: A journey-scoped instance of the known industry-lock theme (20-HR-cohort run); the LLM job-fit itself still reads the full JD text — only this deterministic panel thins out.

title: Candidate-coaching point-of-view leaks into the recruiter report
expected: Report copy consistently addresses the recruiter deciding advance/hold/pass.
got: Several panels address the candidate improving their own CV: gap coaching 'address it in your CV summary or top bullet today' (messages cs/en report.panel.coachMustOne/coachMustMany), salary-evidence hint 'Mention current band … in your CV' (salaryEvidenceHint), a whole 'CV rewrite suggestions' block (JobFitTab.tsx:88-93), and interview-kit STAR scaffolds written as candidate prep (interview.py:1-8 'so the user knows exactly what experience to surface').
ceiling: The v1 candidate-coaching heritage remains until copy is re-audienced; the data itself is recruiter-usable, only the framing misaddresses.
l2_priority: Live: read the cs Job-fit tab as a recruiter; note every second-person-candidate string on screen.
suggested_acceptance: Recruiter-POV copy on recruiter surfaces (e.g. 'ask the candidate to evidence this gap'), with candidate-coaching text reserved for candidate-facing exports.

title: Progress strip is a timer animation dressed as pipeline stages; real per-stage events exist but are unwired
expected: Stage indicators (extract → gemini → profile → scoring → salary → insights) reflect the pipeline's actual progress, or are visually framed as indeterminate.
got: watchAnalysis advances the stage strip on a fixed 1800 ms timer regardless of real state (AnalyzeApi.ts:46-57, comment: 'soft timeline — the pipeline emits one final result'). The Python CLI can emit true SSE stage events via --stream (cli.py:53, pipeline.py _emit) and the task runner forwards per-variant progress only (tasks.ts:97, analyze-run.ts cliArgs:50-59 never pass --stream). On a long run the strip parks on the last stage, implying knowledge it doesn't have.
l2_priority: Live: during a 60-130 s run, compare the strip's claimed stage to the pipeline log's actual stage timings; check whether the strip misleads near the end.
suggested_acceptance: Either wire --stream stage events through the task channel, or restyle the strip as an indeterminate 'working…' so it stops claiming per-stage truth.

title: Growth-target line hardcodes +30% and 'Kč / měsíc' regardless of the estimate's currency and period
expected: Every figure on the salary card is denominated consistently with the estimate (the prompt deliberately emits non-CZK markets: gemini.py:100-101,531).
got: SalaryTab computes target = midpoint*1.3 rounded to 5000 (SalaryTab.tsx:18) and renders it through formatCzk with an i18n label fixed to 'Kč / měsíc' / 'CZK / month' (messages report.panel.growthTarget), while the range beside it correctly uses analysis.salary.currency (SalaryTab.tsx:45). A USD/year estimate would show a mislabeled, wrongly-rounded target. The +30% is also an unexplained magic ratio for a recruiter deciding comp.
l2_priority: Live: analyze a clearly non-Czech-market CV/JD and read the salary card — does the growth target contradict the range's currency/period?
suggested_acceptance: Target formatted in salary.currency/period (shared formatter), the 30% single-sourced with a one-line basis or dropped from the recruiter view.
scope_note: Overlaps backlog idea-615cbc37 (centralize the 30% growth ratio). Low frequency for the ČS-seeded corpus (CZK/month dominant).

title: Ship-bar note: analyze result cache is content-keyed, not tenant-keyed — identical cross-tenant submits share a cached result and skip the meter
expected: Under the public-product bar, per-tenant metering counts each workspace's delivered analyses; cache keys include the tenant where results are billed per tenant.
got: computeCacheKey hashes cv bytes + JD + company + grounding + lang + blind only (analyze-run.ts:97-106); workspace is stamped on the saved row (route.ts:121, analyze-run.ts:184) but not in the key, and a fully-cached run records no meter usage (analyze-run.ts:172-180). No data leak (an identical-bytes submit is required, and the result derives only from those inputs), but tenant B's first run of a document tenant A already analyzed is free and unmetered.
ceiling: Isolation of saved analyses/history is workspace-scoped and sound (history/[slug]/page.tsx:37-40); the seam is metering fairness, not data exposure.
l2_priority: Only if multi-tenant billing goes live: submit the same file from two workspaces and compare meter deltas.
suggested_acceptance: Workspace id joins the cache key (or cached hits still record a metered unit for the consuming tenant).

title: STRENGTH — the hallucinated-matched-skill seam (prior run's major) is now gated at the source, with disclosure
expected: Petra's hard line: no skill appears as matched that isn't in the CV; one fabrication = blocker.
got: verify_skills_in_cv splits LLM matching_skills into verified/withheld against the actual CV text — alias-aware via the taxonomy (JS confirms JavaScript, k8s confirms Kubernetes) plus whole-token literal fallback (ats.py:105-141); the pipeline applies it before any surface (chips, coverage, interview kit) and writes 'Withheld N AI-suggested matching skill(s)…' into the trust ledger instead of dropping silently (pipeline.py:200-210). Closes l1-2026-06-19 finding petra-cvfit-skill-hallucination-seam / EVA-CVJF-1 in code.
l2_priority: Adversarial live check: every matched chip findable in the CV text; try a CV whose JD-adjacent skill appears only as an alias, and one where it doesn't appear at all. Prior-run finding can be marked resolved-verified only with this live evidence.
suggested_acceptance: Zero unverifiable matched chips across 3 live runs; withheld note visible in QualityStrip when triggered.

title: STRENGTH — salary is a basis-carrying number end to end (anchor → cite rule → repair → ledger → gauge)
expected: A salary figure with a band, seniority and market basis — never a naked amount.
got: Deterministic CZK anchor band from data/salary_benchmarks.json (taxonomy.py:286-304) rides the prompt with an explicit cite-or-ignore market rule (gemini.py:524-525,532); company context adjusts with a capped multiplier and appends its own rationale (insights.py:24-78); midpoint is re-derived when out-of-band (pipeline.py:677-679); order/plausibility checks land in the trust ledger (pipeline.py:1065-1092, salary_band.py:33); the UI shows range, period, confidence badge, structure note, rationale bullets, evidence trace, and grounded market evidence with vetted source links (SalaryTab.tsx:26-110).
l2_priority: Live: assert the rendered rationale actually names the anchor/market basis in Czech, not generic filler.
suggested_acceptance: Rationale names band + seniority + market; sanity ledger clean on a plausible CZK band.

title: STRENGTH — JD integrity is guarded on every path; a JD-blind run cannot masquerade as role-specific
expected: Job-fit is computed against this role or not at all.
got: Saved-JD pick detaches the slug on any body-fetch failure (useAnalyzeJdLibrary.ts:50-58,64-74); submit blocks a slug-without-body (useAnalyzeForm.ts:388-391); the prompt nulls job_fit when no JD text arrives (gemini.py:479-483, pipeline.py:187-191); the GitHub deep-dive reads the same JD source and WARNS when the JD couldn't be read instead of silently running JD-blind (runAnalysis.ts:125-146).
suggested_acceptance: Hold: no path produces a role-tagged, JD-blind analysis.

title: STRENGTH — refresh-surviving background run with a real cancel and delivered-work-only metering
expected: A long AI run that doesn't die with the tab, can be stopped, and doesn't bill failures.
got: startTask detaches the run (route.ts:138); the task id is stashed and resumed after refresh (useAnalyzeForm.ts:25,260-281); the poll bails after ~15 s of solid failure instead of spinning (AnalyzeApi.ts:64-74); Cancel DELETEs the task, which SIGKILLs the Python child mid-LLM-call (useAnalyzeForm.ts:197-207, analyze-run.ts:117-121); the ai_candidates unit is debited only for a delivered, non-cached analysis (analyze-run.ts:174-180).
l2_priority: Live: refresh mid-run and confirm re-attach; confirm the Tasks indicator tracks the run (journey L2 item).
suggested_acceptance: Refresh mid-run resumes to the same result; cancel leaves no zombie python.

title: GitHub evidence never reaches the headline verdict — collected, rendered, persisted, but structurally excluded from the analysis it should inform; two disjoint skill vocabularies across adjacent tabs
expected: For an engineer hire, the job-fit verdict/score/risk-flags weigh the candidate's public code evidence (the strongest hard signal Eva holds), or the verdict states it didn't.
got: The deep-dive is a parallel client-fired call (useAnalyzeForm.ts:343-372,405) whose result only joins the UI (ResultPanel.tsx:61-70,170-178) and the saved row (GH1 PATCH useAnalyzeForm.ts:289-302); analyze_profile_with_gemini has no GitHub parameter (gemini.py:439-448), so a CV claiming Kubernetes with zero infra repos still scores on the CV narration and the contradiction must be reconciled by hand. Additionally the GitHub tab's skill space is a hand-rolled 27-bucket alias map (github-analysis/route.ts:111-138) disjoint from the CV tab's data/taxonomy.json — adjacent tabs can disagree on what counts as a match.
l2_priority: Live: engineer CV + ČS JD + real handle; check (a) whether the two tabs visibly disagree on skills/coverage, (b) that the headline summary never references repos, (c) how long the manual reconciliation takes Eva.
suggested_acceptance: The deep-dive result (confirmed_skills / unverified_claims) is fed into the analysis (a second prompt block or a post-pass that annotates job_fit), and both surfaces resolve skills through one taxonomy.

title: Matched-skill verification is circular: LLM claims are checked against the LLM's own extracted text, not the independent pypdf extraction
expected: The trust gate verifies against evidence independent of the model being gated.
got: verify_skills_in_cv receives raw_text = the Gemini payload's own profile.raw_text (pipeline.py:160-166, 200-202), and ats.py's detected_skills/literal checks run over that same text (ats.py:122-141). If the model hallucinates content into its extraction (most plausible on scanned/low-quality PDFs where pypdf returned nothing to compare), the gate self-confirms. The independent pypdf text exists in the same scope (pipeline.py:117) but is unused for verification.
l2_priority: Adversarial live: a scanned/pathological PDF whose pypdf text is empty — check whether extraction-level inventions can surface as 'verified' chips; compare pypdf vs gemini text in the extractor-comparison panel.
suggested_acceptance: When non-empty, the pypdf text participates in verification (skill verified if found in EITHER extraction, flagged when only in the LLM's); when pypdf is empty, the ledger notes verification ran against the model's own read.

title: job_fit.score is a bare clamped LLM scalar — no deterministic reconciliation, unlike the main score's component-sum contract
expected: A fit score Eva can trace: either decomposed like the main score (whose dial is pinned to its component sum) or sanity-checked against the deterministic coverage signal computed in the same result.
got: job_fit.score is clamp(0,100) of the model's number (pipeline.py:696) with narrative-only drivers; nothing reconciles it against keywordCoverage.coverage_percent (ats.py:66) rendered two panels below, and the ResultPanel comment explicitly exempts it from the score-breakdown invariant (JobFitTab.tsx:37-41). A 78-fit with 20% coverage would render without any flag.
l2_priority: Live: a weak-fit candidate — check whether jobFit.score and coverage% diverge visibly and whether any surface flags it.
suggested_acceptance: A sanity check ('Fit score N diverges from deterministic coverage M% — verify') lands in the trust ledger past a threshold, mirroring the score-total check (pipeline.py:998-1030).

title: STRENGTH — the GitHub deep-dive is honest by construction: named evidence basis, disclosed limits, conservative prompt, fail-loud on empty signals
expected: Eva's bar: evidence-based, never pretending to see what it can't.
got: The review prompt states it reads only README/commit-subjects/file NAMES ('You are NOT reading the source code', github-analysis/route.ts:620-633); the payload carries evidenceBasis + a limitations list (route.ts:252-256,540); when every repo bundle comes back empty (rate-limit), it returns an explicit error instead of letting Gemini fabricate a confident review from nothing (route.ts:585-604); job-fit signals disclose trackedSkillCount so 'no gaps' reads as 'no gaps among N tracked' (route.ts:446-453).
l2_priority: Live: confirm the limitations/evidence-basis actually render in the GitHub tab and read clearly.
suggested_acceptance: Keep — this disclosure pattern is the template the headline verdict should adopt when GitHub integration lands.

title: STRENGTH — score contract: the dial is pinned to the component sum and divergence is written into the trust ledger
expected: A score that cannot tell a different story than its own breakdown — director-proof.
got: The displayed total is reconciled to the component sum (format.ts:457-468, ExtractionTab.tsx:33-37, asserted on load ResultPanel.tsx:77-79); the pipeline independently flags a total-vs-breakdown gap beyond tolerance into sanity_checks (pipeline.py:987-1030), and the saved row stores the reconciled total so History can't disagree with the dial (analyze-run.ts:220-229).
suggested_acceptance: Keep; EVA-CVJF-03 asks for the same discipline on job_fit.score.

title: STRENGTH — degradation is disclosed, never silent: a deep-dive that lost its JD warns beside the result; blind mode fails closed rather than leaking identity
expected: When the run has less context than supplied, the user is told; privacy promises hold under failure.
got: A JD file that wouldn't extract yields a visible warning ('Couldn't read the job description, so it's excluded…', runAnalysis.ts:132-146) instead of a silently JD-blind result; blind screening with an unextractable CV refuses to upload the identity-bearing original and says why (gemini.py:489-503, pipeline.py:126-138); every pipeline repair/degradation lands in the QualityStrip ledger (QualityStrip.tsx:17-67).
suggested_acceptance: Keep — the honesty-under-failure pattern is a differentiator; PET-CVJF-01 is the one place the pattern is missing (the silent save).
